summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 49 of cipher-box (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation ECIES unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI) before pushing and opening a PR.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (5 plans, 3 waves, 6 requirements, plan-check passed after one revision). Execution reached mid-Wave 3 — plans 49-01 through 49-03 done, 49-04 dispatched; PR-QA and push not yet started.

repo: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — takes raw key bytes, no owner-vs-recipient distinction — reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move case.
File keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move. `share_keys` entries are keyed by `itemId` (file UUID), not by parent folder; the download path at line 524 resolves by itemId only.
`adoptSharedFolderResult` must be called only once (for the source result). Calling it for the dest result would corrupt the rendered view because the projection filters by shareId only.
Collision policy on `sdkCore.moveItem` is throw, not auto-rename — throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' (sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:346).
`SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist (shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38) must have `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` added; neither was present after Phase 48.
File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from `share_keys keyType:'file-ipns'`, NOT `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` (owner-wrapped; recipient cannot decrypt it).
Private-vault batch move loops single-item `client.moveItem` via `useFileBrowserActions` → `handleBatchMoveConfirm` → `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems`; there is no dedicated SDK batch method.
SDK dist exposes new methods through `client.d.ts` (the class declaration), not `index.d.ts` (barrel re-export only). Initial concern that methods were missing from dist was a false alarm.
The intel API surface script's regex extractor is unpopulated — it produces an empty artifact and can be omitted from planner prompts; RESEARCH.md carries all verified symbol refs instead.
`@internal` on `ensureFolderLoaded` is documentation-only (no access enforcement). Callers can invoke it directly from the web layer without adding a new public alias.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange takes raw sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey/fileIpnsPrivateKey — key-agnostic, reusable for shared-folder move without modification
moveItem throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' on collision — no auto-rename fallback exists
Pick allowlist for SharedFolderClient — required moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree to be added for Phase 49
Reference pattern for resolving file IPNS key from share_keys keyType:'file-ipns' — the correct approach for re-encryption, not FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted

workflow: Sequential plan execution (no worktrees) is safer than parallel worktrees for autonomous/AFK runs — the merge-back protocol is error-prone to hand-drive and concurrent test runs can starve RAM.
After any wave that adds new public SDK methods, the SDK dist must be rebuilt before dispatching web plans that import those methods — web tsc checks the built dist, not source.
The web package has no `typecheck` npm script; the correct command is `tsc -b` run from the web package root.
GSD plan-checker caught a real gap (REQ-3 had no dedicated unit test so its verify step passed vacuously) — running the checker even on first-pass plans is worth it.
CodeRabbit runs twice: CLI review before PR creation (scope: phase diff), then automatically posts a GitHub review after PR creation — use `/resolve-pr-reviews` for the second pass.
Disabling `commit.gpgsign` locally (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) is the right pattern for AFK automated-commit sessions when the global signer (1Password) would block.

friction: 1Password git signing would have wedged all automated commits during the AFK session — required manual intervention to disable signing locally before execution could proceed.
Plan-checker found 2 blockers + 1 warning on first pass, requiring a targeted revision round (the substantive one: REQ-3 unit test was entirely absent from 49-03).
The gsd-tools binary was not on the planner-revision subagent's PATH, so it could not commit its own changes — the orchestrator had to commit them manually.
Intel surface extractor produced an empty artifact (regex unpopulated) — a silent no-op that could mislead if not caught.
Web package lacks a `typecheck` npm script — required exploratory shell commands to discover the right `tsc -b` invocation.
AI-SPEC gate false-positived on the word 'eval' in the e2e requirement text, requiring manual triage to confirm it was a non-blocking false positive.
